action: Rakuten Securities customers: be wary of messages or calls posing as the company or its partners, never share passwords or PINs, and watch for the company's notice.
date_note: Date the company says it learned a third party may have accessed its systems; Security NEXT published on 2026-11-18.
exec: Test-environment data held financial details of millions of brokerage customers, so keep real customer data out of test systems.
plain: Rakuten Securities says an outsider may have reached its systems and some customer details, including income and asset information, may have leaked. It has not confirmed a leak of passwords or PINs.
summary: Rakuten Securities said it learned on November 16 that a third party may have accessed its systems. Test-environment data may have leaked on November 11: details of up to about 4.47 million accounts, and customer codes and login IDs for up to about 11.25 million. No password or PIN leak or unauthorised trades were found as of November 17. On November 19 the company said it received a report-collection order from Japan's Financial Services Agency.
title: Rakuten Securities says test-environment data on up to about 4.47 million accounts may have leaked

validation.note: Security NEXT and ITmedia NEWS (read in full) independently report the company disclosure; ITmedia adds the company explanation that live data was copied to the test server. Rakuten Securities' own 19 Nov press release read: it states receipt of a report-collection order from the FSA that day; the earlier 17 Nov notice was not retrieved.

review.note: Checked 4 sources (Security NEXT, ITmedia, SBbit, Rakuten 19 Nov PDF): dates, up-to 4.47M/11.25M figures, FSA order of 19 Nov, test environment match. Plain said it reports no leak of passwords/PINs; sources say leak not confirmed; reworded.
